justifications.type_expressiveness: RomanError is a proper enum with meaningful variants including InvalidCharacter(char), though the lookup table uses raw (u32, &str) tuples rather than a dedicated struct.
justifications.error_handling: Typed enum with distinct variants for each failure mode, no panics in library code, implements std::error::Error, and uses checked_add defensively.
justifications.api_ergonomics: Reasonable derives and Display/Error impls, but no doc comments on any public item (RomanError, its variants, to_roman, from_roman).
justifications.idiomaticity: Uses iterators, ?, strip_prefix, and pattern matching idiomatically, though the canonical-form check via re-encoding then string comparison is a slightly heavy-handed approach.
